title: Runtime prefill oscillation logbook
content:
Context:
- Personal scratchpad capturing breadcrumbs from the last week investigating a throughput regression that looks correlated with prefill/padding behavior in the runtime runloop.
- Symptoms seen in prod (canary + a few dedicated pods): overall p99 token latency spikes and ~20% effective throughput drop on medium-length requests (200-800 tokens). Short (<100) and very long (>2k) requests largely unaffected.

Timeline (high level):
- 2025-08-29 09:12 UTC: first alerts (paginated) — multiple services hit SLAs for throughput drop.
- 2025-08-29 10:30 UTC: rolled a conservative config change (reduced prefill-padding from 64->16 tokens) on canary, little immediate effect.
- 2025-09-01: ran controlled traffic replay in staging. Observed oscillation in batch sizes at runtime: bursts of tiny batches then large batches causing sequencing overhead.
- 2025-09-03: started deeper trace collection and this doc (owner).

Quick hypotheses (brain-dump):
1) Prefill/padding heuristic triggers frequent path-switching inside the runloop: the prefill estimator thinks more KV needs preloading -> triggers KV warmup -> invalidates cache -> slot reallocation -> microthrottling.
2) Misconfigured max-wait timer for continuous-runloop when prefill is set non-zero: small jitter -> batch flush too quickly -> frequent incomplete batches -> lower GPU utilization.
3) Route-level traffic skew (high fraction of mid-length requests) interacts poorly with batching window + prefill padding making effective batch size drop.
4) A recent kernel selection change (PR #892) introduced subtle latency variance when sequence lengths are near the quantization boundary (512/768).

Commands & traces I ran (raw):
- k8s pod-level logs (filtering for runloop debug):
  kubectl -n inference logs svc-runner-5f6d7 -c runtime --since=1h | rg "runloop|prefill|flush|batch_size" -n
- grep snippets seen:
  [2025-09-01T14:11:02Z] runloop INFO: prefill_estimate=48 target_window_ms=18 slot_alloc=6 flush_reason=timer
  [2025-09-01T14:11:02Z] batching DEBUG: batch_size=3 queued=12 kv_cache_hit_rate=0.22
  [2025-09-01T14:11:02Z] gpu_scheduler INFO: kernel_mode=fast_seq len=520 quant_group=1
  [2025-09-01T14:11:02Z] runloop WARN: flush_reason=slot_starvation prefill_inflight=4

- API-level load tests (replay):
  curl -X POST "https://canary.redwood/api/v1/generate" -H "Authorization: Bearer XXXX" -d @test-corpus-mid.json --trace-ascii trace.txt
  Observed: several requests that should have batched together flushed separately (trace shows separate RPCs to runner).

- System-level telemetry I inspected:
  * token throughput vs batch size distribution (grafana panel): median batch size fell from ~18 -> ~9 during regression window.
  * kv cache hit rate dropped from ~0.83 -> 0.38.
  * GPU utilization delta: -14% during observed window.

Repro experiments (staging) and outcomes:
- Experiment A: disable prefill estimator (force prefill=0) on staging pool.
  Result: batch size recovered to expected medians, throughput back to baseline, KV hit rate unchanged (small bump).
  Implication: prefill estimator likely contributing directly.

- Experiment B: set max_wait_ms=20 -> 60 (wider batching window) while prefill=48.
  Result: batch size improves but latency p99 worsens (timers tradeoff).

- Experiment C: force consistent kernel path (pin quant_group) to test PR #892 hypothesis.
  Result: minor improvement in variance but not enough to explain throughput drop.

Errors and odd logs (copied):
- Timeout/overflow snippets:
  2025-09-01T14:16:40Z ERROR: RequestTimeout: request timed out after 120s, inflight_slots=0
  2025-09-01T14:16:40Z ERROR: AssertionError: expected_batch_size >= 4 (got 0)
  2025-09-01T14:16:40Z WARN: kv_prefill: estimated 72 > sliding_window 32, capping to 32

- Strange interleaving observed in runloop logs:
  - prefill_estimate increases in the same ms that slot allocator splits a batch (suspect race).

Hot leads / deeper traces to collect next:
- Add higher-resolution timestamps in runloop around prefill_estimator -> slot_alloc decisions (nanosecond granularity) to confirm race.
- Add correlation logging between incoming request header (seq_len, user_priority) and which slot/batch they landed in (small, redacted id).
- Replay a focused synthetic workload with mid-length mix (50% 300-600 tokens, 50% <50 tokens) and capture full trace across ingress->runner->gpu.

Temporary mitigations tried/considered:
- Rollback PR #892 to a canary subset (we tried pinning kernel selection, small win but not root cause).
- Conservative policy: set prefill_max to 16 and increase max_wait_ms to 40ms. This was applied to canary and reduced incident noise but hurt p99 for some latency-sensitive customers.
- Consider per-route prefill tuning: disable prefill for routes with high mid-length proportion.

Notes to self / unresolved questions:
- Why does kv_cache_hit_rate drop so sharply when prefill is increased? Are we evicting entries due to temporary over-prefill and then thrashing? Need to profile LRU eviction timing per-shard.
- Is there a scheduling interaction where prefill causes additional memory pressure on CPU side leading to GC pausing in the allocator used by runtime (we've seen small GC spikes aligned with flush events)?
- Could rate-limiter/backpressure signals be inverted when prefill is high — e.g., we think we have content prefetched but actually we spawn more inflight prefill tasks that contend for IO and reduce throughput.

Quick experiment plan (next 48h):
1) Instrument runloop with correlation ids and high-res stamps. (Owner: Aisha)
2) Run synthetic mid-length-mix replay with logged traces and compare 1k traces baseline vs prefill=48. (Owner: Evan)
3) Add lightweight metrics: prefill_inflight_count_gauge, prefill_eviction_count, prefill_task_latency_hist. (Owner: Marina)
4) If reproduces, prepare targeted canary config: prefill=0 for route X for 24h and monitor. (Owner: Ravi)

Useful references / past incidents:
- INFR-221 (2024-11) had similar p99 spikes caused by batching window mis-specified for high-priority routes — journaling that for lessons.
- PR #703: initial prefill estimator implementation notes (see linked GH).

Ideas for long-term fixes:
- Make prefill estimator conservative: require consistent evidence across N windows before increasing prefill size.
- Backpressure: ensure prefill inflight tasks count against an overall slot budget to avoid overcommitting.
- Per-route autopilot: runtime can learn preferred prefill/timeout per route from historical traces.

Misc scratchpad logs (attachments):
- test-corpus-mid.json (payload used for replay) stored in /tmp/replays/test-corpus-mid.json
- trace snippets saved to s3://redwood-debug/traces/prefill-2025-09-03.tgz

If you pick this up: read the staged traces I uploaded (slack thread above) and start with the instrument step. Best place to capture correlation ids is right before runloop slot allocation.

End of notes.

(This is a working doc; will update as new traces come in.)
